briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 18, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Severe Reality of Climate Change and Emergency Warnings
sections.content: Today's climate-related news clearly demonstrates the intensifying threat of climate change globally. Extreme weather phenomena, such as record-breaking heatwaves, extreme droughts, and sudden torrential rainfall reaching 957mm over three days, are occurring in various locations both domestically and internationally, causing immense damage to human lives and agriculture [1, 2, 5, 8, 16, 21, 22, 110, 112, 129]. The agricultural sector, in particular, is suffering severe damage, with the French champagne industry threatened by abnormal high temperatures and agricultural regions in Gyeongbuk facing complex disasters [8, 16]. Furthermore, warnings that butterflies may disappear after bees highlight the severity of ecosystem collapse [11, 118]. The Swiss Association of Cities is urging a nationwide response to climate change and heatwaves, and 20 years of research show that significant impacts have already occurred in northern Canada [121, 122], emphasizing that climate change is no longer a distant future problem but a daily reality [9, 113, 123, 128]. Amidst this situation, the UK Reform Party's remark, "Enjoy the heatwave," has further fueled public criticism against climate change denial [1, 127].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Actions and Efforts Towards Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Even as the climate crisis intensifies, active efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally to transition to a carbon-neutral society. Jincheon County is accelerating its transition to low-carbon smart agriculture [13], and Seongdong-gu proactively responded to climate change adaptation by completing cooling and residential environment improvements for vulnerable households before the heatwave [15, 20, 23]. Gwacheon City encouraged citizens to practice carbon neutrality through a 10-minute lights-out campaign on 'Energy Day' [24, 25, 34, 57], and Gimhae City connected everyday carbon neutrality with neighborly love by donating carbon neutrality point incentives [26, 27, 28, 38, 45, 53]. Furthermore, Jangsu County is leading the way in carbon neutrality by expanding the use of domestic timber [31, 33, 37, 39, 47, 51], and the role of corporations is also growing, with CATL achieving its carbon neutrality goal for key operations by 2025 and presenting a roadmap for its 2035 value chain target [40, 59]. In addition, movements towards achieving carbon neutrality are active in various fields, including seminars hosted by the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute, joint research by five power generation companies and four universities [48, 49], and efforts to cultivate specialized carbon neutrality professionals [35, 36].

sections.title: 🌱 Challenges for Renewable Energy Expansion and Stable Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a core pillar of climate change response, and efforts to expand it are active in various local governments across the country. Muju County has been selected for the Renewable Energy Convergence Support Project, expanding its energy self-sufficiency infrastructure [62, 66, 71, 72, 74, 76, 82, 88, 104], and Goyang City is promoting the introduction of 'Goyang-style Solar Pension' to expand citizen-participatory renewable energy projects [64, 78, 94, 95, 98, 102, 107]. Haenam County is focusing on establishing policies that consider regional co-prosperity, such as initiating the development of a 'Haenam-type Renewable Energy Management System' that includes agricultural preservation and the return of profits to residents in large-scale solar power development [65, 69, 77, 85, 89, 90, 92, 96, 97, 100, 105, 109]. Meanwhile, alongside the expansion of renewable energy supply, the establishment of a stable power grid is emerging as a critical challenge. China, for instance, faces severe issues of grid inadequacy and output curtailment due to the expansion of renewable energy [63, 80], and Germany has also reported grid bottlenecks resulting from increased renewable energy capacity [70], which holds significant implications for Korea's power system. In this situation, KOSPO (Korea Southern Power Co., Ltd.) is seeking innovative solutions by embarking on the establishment of a carbon-free power ecosystem that links solar power, green hydrogen, and hydrogen power generation for the first time in Korea [99].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Policies and Public Awareness for Climate Crisis Response
sections.content: Responding to the climate crisis requires multifaceted efforts, including the establishment of government policies and raising public awareness. The National Assembly Busan Library is hosting a 'Climate Crisis' exhibition to draw public attention [18], and Yeosu City expressed its regional commitment by holding a short-form video contest wishing to host the Climate Change Conference on the South Coast [17, 29, 55]. From a policy perspective, the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act, which includes reduction pathways beyond 2030, has been established, but its impact on corporate targets is analyzed to be limited [32]. Specific policy discussions are also underway, such as introducing an upper limit for setback distance regulations for renewable energy facilities [73]. Furthermore, at the 12th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand policy debate, discussions included the transition to an electric nation and forecasts for electricity demand and renewable energy supply [103], indicating deep consideration for setting long-term energy policy directions. Notably, public awareness of climate change is increasing, with two-thirds of viewers demanding that extreme weather reports include climate change narratives [125]. Moreover, the German Social Democratic Party is even pushing for constitutional amendments to address heatwaves and the climate crisis [120], demonstrating that governments and civil societies worldwide are actively participating in responding to the climate crisis [3, 7, 12, 111, 114, 116, 117, 119, 124, 126].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severe reality of climate change, while also demonstrating the ongoing diverse efforts both domestically and internationally to overcome it. We hope that interest and action regarding climate change will continue in the future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
